decisions.reason: As a 2018 launch that builds on the established offer, there is no clear evidence of results below aspiration yet, and a growing, hiring, R&D-active firm would typically use available slack to keep testing it for another period.
This modular waste-to-energy extension sits squarely in the firm's core technological domain, so with no visible shortfall and with industry growth the boundedly rational choice is to retain it.

The waste-oil-to-energy plant is strongly aligned with the firm's established business and was prominent enough to have its own page, so management would likely judge it worth continuing under current slack and uncertainty.

Although somewhat newer and only close to the core offer, plastic-waste-to-fuel technology fits the firm's long-run search in circular and energy solutions, so absent clear underperformance it would be kept.
